name: Jorai
title: Head of the tribe of Gad
summary: Jorai was one of the heads of the tribe of Gad mentioned in 1 Chronicles. He is listed among the family heads of Gad who lived in the region of Bashan. His mention is limited to the genealogies in the books of Chronicles, but he represents part of Israel's tribal history and organization.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Gad
keyEvents.description: Jorai is listed as one of the heads of the tribe of Gad in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles. He belonged to the leadership among the Gadites who lived in the territories of Gilead and Bashan.

keyEvents.title: The settlement of the Gadites in Bashan
keyEvents.description: Jorai and the other heads of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, which was a fertile land east of the Jordan. Their genealogies were recorded during the reigns of Jotham, king of Judah, and Jeroboam, king of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Genealogical Records during Jotham and Jeroboam
keyEvents.description: The genealogies of the Gadites, including Jorai, were recorded in connection with official censuses under King Jotham of Judah and King Jeroboam II of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Military Strength of the Gadites
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Gad, to which Jorai belonged, was known for its skilled warriors. The tribe had a strong military tradition and protected Israel's eastern border regions.
